label: early original-phase step after a prefix rich in h/x/e/f/d/3/1/b
explanation: Fires mostly during the original phase (88% of mass), at positions t=2..5 (85% of mass; peak t=3), never at t=0. Whether it fires depends on which tokens came before: it is much more likely when the earlier tokens (especially first_tok, prev_tok and prev2_tok) come from {h, x, e, f, d, 3, 1, b}. The current input is most often t, x or o, then a, z, g, y, c. On dev, requiring all earlier tokens to be from that set at t=2..4 raises precision to about 0.6 but drops recall to 0.17, so the response looks graded and combinatorial over the prefix rather than a crisp rule. It is weak in the delimiter and copy phases (about 11% of mass, mostly recall_idx 1-2) and almost silent after t=6 in the original phase. Most false positives have the right position and a partly matching prefix but do not cross the threshold. I did not establish what controls magnitude beyond the top examples, which are concentrated at t=3-4 after h/x-heavy prefixes.
